body: The root cause is that, "minimal" mode only [inject metadata](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/RemoteCache.java;l=604) of output which is an instance of `Artifact` into the filesystem. However, [`test.xml`](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/test/TestRunnerAction.java;l=282) is an instance of [`BasicActionInput`](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/actions/ActionInputHelper.java;l=61) which is not a subclass of `Artifact`. Hence, Bazel won't know the existence of that file.

issue.title: Change test.xml from BasicActionInput to Artifact so it's metadata can be injected

This is achieved by adding test.xml to TestRunnerAction's outputs which means test.xml becomes a mandatory output of TestRunnerAction just like test.log.

test.xml should always be generated by either test actions or the separated spawn action enabled by --experimental_split_xml_generation.

Fixes #12554.

issue.body:
### Description of the bug:


I'm trying to make Bazel unconditionally download the `test.xml` output files of the test runs from the remote cache and whether this works is hit-or-miss.

The scenario I'm trying is:

```
$ bazel test --config=remote-only --remote_download_regex='.*/test.xml' //some:test
$ fd --follow test.xml bazel-testlogs/some                                                                       
bazel-testlogs/some/test/test.xml    <-- This is sometimes missing
```

Here is what I have found:

* The `test.xml` is downloaded if the test results are NOT cached yet (`--nocache_test_results`).
* The `test.xml` is NOT downloaded if the test results are cached.
* The `test.xml` is correctly downloaded in either case if I run `bazel clean` first.
* Running with "remote download all" causes the `test.xml` to be downloaded in all cases.

This seems like a bug.

I've also found https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/12554 which is NOT related to this problem but the discussion there seems to imply that `test.xml` is "special" so it wouldn't surprise me if it isn't accounted for somehow.
